title: What should an alarm MEAN?
question: Should eating another CREATURE raise an alarm, or should alarm mean only "I was attacked"?
context_md:
Your two rulings are shipped: **creatures do not attack plants**, and **eating a plant raises no alarm**. Your longant bed, same seed, 40,000 frames — the pictures are just so you can see it landed. **The question below is the ask.**

You found the loop yourself and it was the whole of it: on that bed **100% of every swing and every cell taken by the jaw was at a plant**, and the jaw was removing **9 of every 10 cells** a colony took off a living plant while feeding on none of them.

Alarm is the only thing in the engine that makes an ant reach for the fight verb, so what writes it decides what a colony comes running for. Three moments can write one:

| the moment | raises an alarm? |
|---|---|
| **an ant is bitten by the fight verb** | yes — not in question |
| **an ant is EATEN by another ant** | **your call** |
| **a plant is grazed** | no — your ruling, shipped |

**What I would ship if you have no strong preference:** an alarm whenever a *living animal* is bitten, whichever verb did it — from the victim's side, being eaten **is** being attacked. That excludes plants and corpses and keeps the shout for the one thing worth running to.

**And it costs you nothing to decide either way today:** over three 40,000-frame runs of this bed an ant ate another ant **zero** times. One colony has no strangers to eat. It starts to matter the moment two colonies share a box — which is now the default.

items.caption: 60 plants standing. 7,442 swings at plants, 5,071 plant cells smashed and eaten by nobody.
